lessons.subject: English
lessons.title: Fronted adverbials
lessons.summary: Start a sentence with words that say when, where or how.
lessons.curriculum: Year 4 English: use fronted adverbials, with commas after them
pages: An adverbial tells you when, where or how something happens.
A fronted adverbial comes at the start of a sentence. For example: ‘Later that day, we went to the park.’
Put a comma after a fronted adverbial. For example: ‘Without a sound, the cat crept past.’

check.question: Which sentence uses a fronted adverbial correctly?
options: Before lunch, we read a story.
We read a story, before lunch.
Before lunch we, read a story.
check.explanation: ‘Before lunch’ comes first, with a comma after it.

lessons.subject: Maths
lessons.title: Times tables up to 12 × 12
lessons.summary: Practise times tables facts up to 12 × 12.
lessons.curriculum: Year 4 maths: recall multiplication and division facts for multiplication tables up to 12 × 12
pages: By the end of Year 4, you should know all the times tables up to 12 × 12. In Year 4, you take a short online check of them.
Use facts you know to work out new ones. 6 × 7 is double 3 × 7. 3 × 7 = 21, so 6 × 7 = 42.

check.question: What is 7 × 8?
check.explanation: 7 × 8 = 56. One way to remember it: 5, 6, 7, 8, as in 56 = 7 × 8.

lessons.subject: Science
lessons.title: Simple circuits
lessons.summary: Build a circuit and find out which materials let electricity through.
lessons.curriculum: Year 4 science: construct a simple series circuit, and recognise some common conductors and insulators
pages: A circuit is a path that electricity flows around. A simple circuit has a cell, wires and a bulb.
The circuit must be a complete loop. If there is a gap, the bulb will not light. A switch opens and closes a gap.
Conductors let electricity flow through them. Most metals, like copper, are good conductors.
Insulators, like plastic and rubber, do not let electricity through. Wires are covered in plastic to keep you safe.

check.question: Which material is a good conductor?
check.explanation: Copper is a metal, and most metals are good conductors.

lessons.subject: History
lessons.title: The Romans in Britain
lessons.summary: Find out how the Roman Empire changed Britain.
lessons.curriculum: Key stage 2 history: the Roman Empire and its impact on Britain
pages: In AD 43, the Roman army invaded Britain. Britain was part of the Roman Empire for more than 350 years.
In about AD 60, Boudica, queen of the Iceni tribe, led a revolt against the Romans. The Romans defeated her army.
The Romans built straight roads, towns and public baths. Many towns began as Roman towns, such as London.
In AD 122, Emperor Hadrian ordered a long wall across the north of England. You can still see parts of Hadrian's Wall today.

check.question: Who led a revolt against the Romans in Britain?
check.explanation: Boudica, queen of the Iceni, led a revolt in about AD 60.
